<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #53284: use the rendered Qwen3 prompt to recognize an already closed reasoning block, so a plain generated answer is returned as content rather than reasoning.

Updated on October 6: rebased onto `b0b23a48d4` and resolved the conflicts with #58604. The batched path keeps #58604's per-prompt parser and `set_prompt_token_ids()` call and parses through `parse_with_prompt()`. The legacy `ReasoningParser` interface is unchanged.

## Claims

- Qwen3's current-turn prompt state is respected in Chat and Responses (streaming and non-streaming), and in Batch Chat; historical reasoning markers do not select the new turn's state.
- Prompt-closed answers have zero reasoning tokens; explicit thinking and cumulative streaming reasoning accounting remain intact.
- Existing `parse()` signatures and legacy reasoning plugins remain compatible. Responses still reuses streamed output items instead of reparsing them.

## Validation

**October 6 rebase (`adf9f1104f`), agent-run:** the suite below produced 704 passed, 1 xfailed (the same existing xfail). `test_batched_parser_receives_prompt_token_ids` was folded into #58604's `test_batched_parser_receives_each_prompt_prefix`, which now checks both `set_prompt_token_ids()` and the `prompt_token_ids` passed to `parse_with_prompt()`. Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass. The human-run results below are for the previous revision.

Revision tested: `7f907531483eef3ff7415c1f4ee9ee92f01599b9`.

- **Human-run regression:** 702 passed, 1 xfailed, 40 warnings in 87.99 seconds. The submitting human reviewed the changes and personally ran the command below before authorizing this update.
- **Agent-run regression:** the same suite produced 702 passed, 1 xfailed, 40 warnings in 123.69 seconds.
- All changed-file pre-commit hooks, Python 3.10 mypy, manual Python 3.12 mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. Static checks were rerun immediately before this update.
- The xfail is the existing `test_zero_delta_items_should_preserve_streaming_lifecycle`; warnings are Torch/xgrammar deprecations. These are local results, not an upstream CI pass.

<details>
<summary>Regression and static-check commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py \
  tests/parser/test_parse.py \
  tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py \
  tests/parser/test_harmony.py \
  tests/parser/test_streaming.py \
  tests/reasoning/test_qwen3_reasoning_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_parsable_context_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_nonstreaming_parser_receives_prompt_token_ids \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_streaming_reasoning_usage_counts_across_deltas \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::test_batched_parser_receives_each_prompt_prefix \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::test_batched_harmony_response_format_uses_structural_tag \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py::test_batch_rejects_kv_transfer_prompt_token_ids \
  -q

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run \
  --from-ref bcee730b1a9d25f0fd283a0ef6c19133ebeebf4f --to-ref HEAD
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
git diff bcee730b1a9d25f0fd283a0ef6c19133ebeebf4f HEAD --check
```

Tests extend existing suites already covered by the parser/reasoning and OpenAI entrypoint Buildkite jobs; the test-tethering hook passed.

</details>

### Model-output validation

Agent-run, on one RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` revision `15852e8c16360a2fea060d615a32b45270f8a8fc`, BF16, TP=1, MRV2, eager execution, max model length 2048, temperature 0.

With the official template and `enable_thinking` omitted, a deterministic real-tokenizer/parser comparison for the same generated `OK` gave:

| Parser revision | reasoning | content | reasoning tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base `bcee730b1a` | `OK` | null | 1 |
| This PR `7f90753148` | null | `OK` | 0 |

That baseline comparison is parser-level, not a second GPU server run. On the patched GPU server all seven HTTP smoke cases passed:

| Case | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Chat, nonstreaming, include reasoning | `OK` content, null reasoning, 0 reasoning tokens |
| Chat, nonstreaming, exclude reasoning | `OK` content, null reasoning, 0 reasoning tokens |
| Chat, streaming | `OK` content, no reasoning delta, 0 reasoning tokens |
| Chat, explicit `enable_thinking=true` | Reasoning preserved; 128 generated tokens counted as reasoning before length truncation |
| Batch Chat | `OK` and `YES` content, null reasoning |
| Responses, nonstreaming | `OK` output text, no reasoning item, 0 reasoning tokens |
| Responses, streaming | Streamed `OK` equals completed output, no reasoning item, 0 reasoning tokens |

Environment limitation: the default FlashInfer GDN warmup encountered a missing `cutlass` dependency. The successful smoke run explicitly used Triton GDN and the native sampler; the installed FlashInfer JIT also reported an SM12 toolchain warning. This validates output classification in the configuration below, not the default FlashInfer path or a general accuracy/performance benchmark.

Python 3.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu130. Native extensions came from official cu130 artifacts at `24fb5fc08c`; that revision differs from the tested base only in two documentation files. The tested source is the PR revision above.

<details>
<summary>GPU server command and seven-case client</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 .venv/bin/vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
  --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --enforce-eager \
  --additional-config '{"gdn_prefill_backend":"triton"}' \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080
```

Save the client below as `smoke_qwen35.py` outside the checkout and run it with `.venv/bin/python /path/to/smoke_qwen35.py`. It printed `All 7 serving smoke cases passed.`

```python
"""Local HTTP smoke checks for the prompt-closed Qwen3 parser fix."""

import json

import httpx


MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B"
client = httpx.Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:18080", timeout=180)
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly the word OK."}]
chat = dict(model=MODEL, messages=messages, max_tokens=32, temperature=0, seed=0)


def post(path, payload):
    response = client.post(path, json=payload)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()


def events(path, payload):
    with client.stream("POST", path, json=payload) as response:
        response.raise_for_status()
        for line in response.iter_lines():
            if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]":
                yield json.loads(line[6:])


def record(name, result):
    print(json.dumps({"case": name, **result}, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)


for include in (True, False):
    result = post("/v1/chat/completions", {**chat, "include_reasoning": include})
    message = result["choices"][0]["message"]
    record(f"chat_include_reasoning_{include}", result)
    assert message["content"].strip() == "OK"
    assert not message.get("reasoning")
    assert result["usage"]["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == 0

content, reasoning, usage = "", "", None
for event in events(
    "/v1/chat/completions",
    {**chat, "stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}},
):
    if event.get("usage"):
        usage = event["usage"]
    for choice in event.get("choices", []):
        content += choice["delta"].get("content") or ""
        reasoning += choice["delta"].get("reasoning") or ""
record("chat_stream", dict(content=content, reasoning=reasoning, usage=usage))
assert content.strip() == "OK" and not reasoning
assert usage["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == 0

result = post(
    "/v1/chat/completions",
    {**chat, "max_tokens": 128, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
)
record("chat_explicit_thinking", result)
assert result["choices"][0]["message"].get("reasoning")
assert result["usage"]["completion_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] > 0

result = post(
    "/v1/chat/completions/batch",
    {
        **chat,
        "messages": [
            messages,
            [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly the word YES."}],
        ],
    },
)
record("batch_chat", result)
assert [c["message"]["content"].strip() for c in result["choices"]] == ["OK", "YES"]
assert all(not c["message"].get("reasoning") for c in result["choices"])

responses = dict(
    model=MODEL,
    input="Reply with exactly the word OK.",
    max_output_tokens=32,
    temperature=0,
)


def response_text(result):
    assert not any(item["type"] == "reasoning" for item in result["output"])
    assert result["usage"]["output_tokens_details"]["reasoning_tokens"] == 0
    return "".join(
        part["text"]
        for item in result["output"]
        if item["type"] == "message"
        for part in item["content"]
        if part["type"] == "output_text"
    )


result = post("/v1/responses", responses)
record("responses", result)
assert response_text(result).strip() == "OK"

stream_text = ""
completed = None
for event in events("/v1/responses", {**responses, "stream": True}):
    if event["type"] == "response.output_text.delta":
        stream_text += event["delta"]
    elif event["type"] == "response.completed":
        completed = event["response"]
assert completed is not None
record("responses_stream", dict(stream_text=stream_text, response=completed))
assert response_text(completed) == stream_text
assert stream_text.strip() == "OK"
print("All 7 serving smoke cases passed.", flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

The template can close `<think>...</think>` without setting `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. Complete-output parsing previously lost the rendered prompt context and started from the configured default reasoning state.

The shared change addresses that missing context in the unified parsing contract and its serving callers. `Parser.parse_with_prompt()` defaults to the existing `parse()` behavior; `DelegatingParser` supplies the fallback for legacy parsers. `ReasoningParser` itself is unchanged. The Qwen-specific current-turn marker scan stays in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`. The adapter preserves the selected state when replaying tokens for reasoning counts. There are no scheduler, model-runner, kernel, or dependency changes, and no throughput claim.

The rebase preserves upstream's Responses streamed-item reuse and Batch Chat tests. Added coverage includes direct and delegated parsing, streaming finalization/counting, history/tool-example boundaries, prompt propagation, and a legacy parser with no prompt-aware hook. The capability is documented in its interface docstring; no new user-facing configuration is introduced.

### Duplicate-work check

Rechecked #53284, its comments, and open PRs by issue number and prompt/reasoning keywords before this update. This updates the existing PR rather than opening another.

The related Gemma4 work and shared-plumbing distinction are also recorded in [the issue scope update](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53284#issuecomment-5929562421).

- Merged #56200 derives end detection from the grammar; it does not implement the complete-output prompt propagation and Qwen initial-state/counting fix here. The distinction was already explained in [the issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53284#issuecomment-5617771488).
- Draft #50015 addresses Gemma4's half-open thought channel. It overlaps the generic prompt plumbing, but deliberately leaves Qwen non-streaming behavior unchanged and extends `parse()` directly. This PR handles Qwen's closed think block, keeps existing `parse()` signatures, and includes Batch Chat and reasoning-count coverage. The shared API/plumbing should be reconciled if both changes proceed; this PR does not claim to fix Gemma4.
- #58911 addresses buffered content lost after a generated reasoning end with no tool parser, not prompt-closed initialization.
- #59263 forwards reasoning configuration to the Batch Chat engine-side structured-output gate; #50676 preserves generated output token IDs during engine parsing. Neither implements Qwen prompt-closed output classification.

### AI assistance and accountability

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, local test execution, GPU smoke validation, and PR preparation. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines, ran the regression suite reported above, and authorized this update. GPU and static-check results are explicitly agent-run; they are not represented as human-run or upstream CI results.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

        completed = event["response"]
assert completed is not None
record("responses_stream", dict(stream_text=stream_text, response=completed))
assert response_text(completed) == stream_text
assert stream_text.strip() == "OK"
print("All 7 serving smoke cases passed.", flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

The template can close `<think>...</think>` without setting `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. Complete-output parsing previously lost the rendered prompt context and started from the configured default reasoning state.

The shared change addresses that missing context in the unified parsing contract and its serving callers. `Parser.parse_with_prompt()` defaults to the existing `parse()` behavior; `DelegatingParser` supplies the fallback for legacy parsers. `ReasoningParser` itself is unchanged. The Qwen-specific current-turn marker scan stays in `vllm/parser/qwen3.py`. The adapter preserves the selected state when replaying tokens for reasoning counts. There are no scheduler, model-runner, kernel, or dependency changes, and no throughput claim.

The rebase preserves upstream's Responses streamed-item reuse and Batch Chat tests. Added coverage includes direct and delegated parsing, streaming finalization/counting, history/tool-example boundaries, prompt propagation, and a legacy parser with no prompt-aware hook. The capability is documented in its interface docstring; no new user-facing configuration is introduced.

### Duplicate-work check

Rechecked #53284, its comments, and open PRs by issue number and prompt/reasoning keywords before this update. This updates the existing PR rather than opening another.

The related Gemma4 work and shared-plumbing distinction are also recorded in [the issue scope update](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53284#issuecomment-5929562421).

- Merged #56200 derives end detection from the grammar; it does not implement the complete-output prompt propagation and Qwen initial-state/counting fix here. The distinction was already explained in [the issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53284#issuecomment-5617771488).
- Draft #50015 addresses Gemma4's half-open thought channel. It overlaps the generic prompt plumbing, but deliberately leaves Qwen non-streaming behavior unchanged and extends `parse()` directly. This PR handles Qwen's closed think block, keeps existing `parse()` signatures, and includes Batch Chat and reasoning-count coverage. The shared API/plumbing should be reconciled if both changes proceed; this PR does not claim to fix Gemma4.
- #58911 addresses buffered content lost after a generated reasoning end with no tool parser, not prompt-closed initialization.
- #59263 forwards reasoning configuration to the Batch Chat engine-side structured-output gate; #50676 preserves generated output token IDs during engine parsing. Neither implements Qwen prompt-closed output classification.

### AI assistance and accountability

OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, local test execution, GPU smoke validation, and PR preparation. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines, ran the regression suite reported above, and authorized this update. GPU and static-check results are explicitly agent-run; they are not represented as human-run or upstream CI results.

👋 Hi! Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.

</details>

Rebased onto current main (`b0b23a48d4`) to resolve the conflicts with #58604. In the batched path I kept #58604's per-prompt parser and its `set_prompt_token_ids()` call and parse through `parse_with_prompt()`. #58604's batched test now checks both, and the parser/reasoning/Responses suite from the description passes locally (704 passed, 1 existing xfail).

#58604 also added a `Parser.set_prompt_token_ids()` hook. If you'd prefer a single mechanism, I'm happy to move this PR onto that hook instead of the separate `parse_with_prompt()`.
